title: CSL100 Introduction to Programming (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL100 - Introduction to Programming (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 1, 4.5 Credits. Topics: Basics of programming using C; Basic UNIX commands, Primitives and Datatypes, Arithmetic operations, Input and output functions; Conditional statement; Loops, Introduction to Functions, Macros, Recursion, Arrays, Strings, Dynamic Memory Allocation, Pointers, Complex Data Types, File Handling, Introduction to Linked List, sorting, Searching, Bitwise Operator.

title: MAL100 Mathematics-I (Part 1)
text: Course: MAL100 - Mathematics-I (Mathematics). Semester 1, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Real number system: Sequences: Convergence of a sequence, Sandwich theorem, Cauchy sequences, subsequence, monotone sequences, monotone convergence theorem; Series: Convergence of infinite series, comparison test, Cauchy condensation test, ratio test, root test, Leibnitz test.

title: MAL100 Mathematics-I (Part 2)
text: Course: MAL100 - Mathematics-I (Mathematics). Semester 1, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Functions of one variable: Limits and continuity of functions, intermediate value property, differentiability, local maxima and minima, Rolles theorem, mean value theorem; Integration: Definite integrals, fundamental theorems of calculus, improper integrals.

title: MAL100 Mathematics-I (Part 3)
text: Course: MAL100 - Mathematics-I (Mathematics). Semester 1, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Functions of two variables: Limit, continuity, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient, differentiability, chain rule, tangent planes, maxima and minima, Lagrange multiplier; Multiple integrals: Double and triple integrals, Green theorem, vector fields.

title: MAL101 Mathematics-II (Part 1)
text: Course: MAL101 - Mathematics-II (Mathematics). Semester 2, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Systems of linear equations: Elementary operations, row-reduced echelon matrices, Gauss elimination, LU factorization, linear independence, rank, solutions of linear systems; Vector spaces: Subspaces, spanning space, bases and dimensions; Linear transformations: Matrix representations, range space, rank, null space, nullity theorem, invertibility.

title: MAL101 Mathematics-II (Part 2)
text: Course: MAL101 - Mathematics-II (Mathematics). Semester 2, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors: Hermitian, unitary matrices, eigen bases; Diagonalization: Cayley-Hamilton theorem, quadratic form; Inner product spaces: Orthonormal bases, Gram-Schmidt process; Differential Equations: First Order ODE, Lipschitz condition, Picard theorem; Linear differential equations: Wronskian, higher order constant coefficients, Cauchy-Euler equations, Laplace Transform.

title: ECL101 Basic Electronics Engineering (Part 1)
text: Course: ECL101 - Basic Electronics Engineering (Electronics & Communication Engineering). Semester 2, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Semiconductor Diode, V-I characteristics, Half-Wave and Full-Wave Rectifier Circuits; Transistors: Bipolar Junction Transistor, MOSFET: Biasing, Small Signal model, Amplifiers; Operational Amplifiers: Ideal Op-Amp, applications (rectifiers/clipping, switching); ADC implementation.

title: ECL101 Basic Electronics Engineering (Part 2)
text: Course: ECL101 - Basic Electronics Engineering (Electronics & Communication Engineering). Semester 2, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Logic Gates and Combinational Circuits: Number Systems and Binary Codes, Boolean Algebra, DeMorgans Theorems, SOP and POS Forms, K-Map Method, Combinational Logic Circuits, Half and Full adder-subtractor, Comparators, Multiplexers, Decoders/encoders; Synchronous and Ripple Counters; Communications overview.

title: CSL201 Discrete Mathematics (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL201 - Discrete Mathematics (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 3, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Sets, relations, functions, Equivalence and Partial order relations; Formal logic: Propositional logic and truth tables, normal forms, Predicates and Quantification; Notion of proof: proof techniques, Mathematical Induction; Combinatorics: Basic counting techniques, Pigeonhole principle, countable and uncountable sets, recurrence relations, Inclusion-exclusion principle.

title: CSL201 Discrete Mathematics (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL201 - Discrete Mathematics (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 3, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Graph theory: Graph terminology, representation, Isomorphism, trees, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, Graph coloring, Planar graphs; Number theory: Divisibility, GCD, Euclidean algorithm, Fundamental theorem of arithmetic, Modular arithmetic; Group theory: Groups, subgroups, cyclic groups, permutation groups.

title: CSL202 Data Structures (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL202 - Data Structures (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 3, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Stacks, Queues, Lists; Sorting and Searching; Trees, Tree Traversals; Heaps, Binary Search; Binary Search Trees, Balanced BSTs; Graphs: Representations, Depth First Search, Breadth First Search.

title: CSP203 Software Tools & Technologies Lab (Part 1)
text: Course: CSP203 - Software Tools & Technologies Lab (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 3, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Basics of Linux: Linux commands – text editors; Scripting languages; Web programming; Plotting tools; Document processing tools; Version control systems (Git); Debuggers, such as gdb; Containerization with Docker.

title: MAL403 Probability and Statistics (Part 1)
text: Course: MAL403 - Probability and Statistics (Mathematics). Semester 3, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Introduction to set algebra, sigma algebra, Borel sigma algebra, sequence of sets and limits; Axiomatic definition of probability, probability space, conditional probability, Bayes rule, independence; Random variables, distribution functions, PMF and PDF, expectation, moments, MGF, Markov and Chebyshev inequality.

title: MAL403 Probability and Statistics (Part 2)
text: Course: MAL403 - Probability and Statistics (Mathematics). Semester 3, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Joint distributions, marginal and conditional distributions, covariance and correlation, Central Limit Theorem, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing.

title: CSL251 Computer Organization and Architecture (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL251 - Computer Organization and Architecture (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 4, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Overview of basic digital building blocks, truth tables, basic structure of digital computer, number representation; Machine Instructions and Program: Assembly language programming; Arithmetic Unit: Building blocks for ALU, adder, subtractor, shifter, multiplication/division circuits, microprogramming, hardwired control.

title: CSL251 Computer Organization and Architecture (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL251 - Computer Organization and Architecture (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 4, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Memory organization: ROM, RAM, cache memories, cache coherence, virtual memory, secondary storage; Input/Output: I/O subblock, interrupts, polling, DMA; Pipelining: Instruction pipelines, hazards.

title: CSL252 Design and Analysis of Algorithms (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL252 - Design and Analysis of Algorithms (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 4, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Algorithm analysis: worst and average case, recurrences and asymptotes; Sorting and selection algorithms; Randomized techniques, Divide and Conquer; Dynamic programming and greedy algorithms; Graph algorithms: BFS, DFS and applications, MSTs, shortest paths; NP-Complete problems and Approximation Algorithms.

title: CSL253 Theory of Computation (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL253 - Theory of Computation (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 4, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Alphabets, languages, finite state machines (DFA, NFA); Context Free Grammars and Context-Free Languages, Parse trees, PushDown Automata, CYK algorithm; Turing machines and variants; Undecidability theory, Halting problem, Space and Time complexity, NP-Completeness.

title: CSL301 Operating Systems (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL301 - Operating Systems (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Introduction to OS, Virtualization, Concurrency, Persistence; CPU Virtualization: Process, Process API, PCB, CPU Scheduling, Multilevel feedback queue; Memory Virtualization: Address space, Memory API, address translation, segmentation, paging, TLBs, replacement policies, swapping; Concurrency: threads, Thread API, locks, condition variables, semaphores, concurrency bugs.

title: CSL301 Operating Systems (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL301 - Operating Systems (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Persistence: I/O devices, Hard disks, RAID, file systems; OS Security: Authentication, access control; Tools: xv6.

title: CSL302 Compiler Design (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL302 - Compiler Design (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Compiler structure: analysis-synthesis model of compilation, phases of compiler, tool-based approach; Lexical analysis (lex/flex); Syntax analysis (LL, LR, LALR parsers, yacc/bison); Syntax-directed translation; Type checking and semantic analysis; Run-time storage administration; Intermediate code generation; Machine-independent optimizations; Target code generation.

title: CSL303 Database Management Systems (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL303 - Database Management Systems (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Database System Concepts: Data models, schemas, instances, architecture; Relational Algebra: SELECT, PROJECT, set operations, JOIN, DIVISION; Entity-Relationship (ER) and Enhanced ER (EER) modeling, relational mapping; Normalization: Functional dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF.

title: CSL303 Database Management Systems (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL303 - Database Management Systems (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Database programming: SQL (DDL, DML, triggers, views), transaction management, ACID properties, indexing (B-trees, hashing).

title: CSL304 Artificial Intelligence (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL304 - Artificial Intelligence (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Introduction and Problem solving by search: State Space, Graph Search, A*, Heuristics, Adversarial Game Playing, Constraint Satisfaction; Automated Reasoning: Propositional and first-order logic, resolution refutation, knowledge representation; Planning: State-space and plan space planning; Reasoning under uncertainty: Probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian networks, Fuzzy logic.

title: CSL304 Artificial Intelligence (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL304 - Artificial Intelligence (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 5, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Reinforcement Learning: MDP, Q-Learning.

title: CSL351 Computer Networks (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL351 - Computer Networks (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Layered architecture, packet switching, performance metrics; Application layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, P2P, CDN; Transport Layer: TCP, UDP, flow control, congestion control, QUIC; Socket Programming; Network Layer: IPv4, IPv6, addressing, CIDR, NAT, routing algorithms (OSPF, BGP), ICMP, ARP.

title: CSL351 Computer Networks (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL351 - Computer Networks (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 4.0 Credits. Topics: Data Link Layer: framing, error detection/correction, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA, Ethernet, Wi-Fi; Network security basics, SDN.

title: CSP352 AI-Augmented Software Development (Part 1)
text: Course: CSP352 - AI-Augmented Software Development (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 3.0 Credits. Topics: LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in software lifecycle, testing, debugging, code generation, limitations; Prompting as interface design: Structured prompting, task specification; LLMs as software components: API integration, context handling, schema validation, retries; Agentic workflows: ReAct patterns, planner-executor, tool calling, memory management.

title: CSP352 AI-Augmented Software Development (Part 2)
text: Course: CSP352 - AI-Augmented Software Development (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Observability, test harnesses, safety, governance, and capstone system development.

title: CSL512 Parallel Algorithms (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL512 - Parallel Algorithms (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Models of parallel computation: PRAM models, interconnection networks, performance analysis; Basic parallel techniques: Matrix multiplication, parallel sorting, searching, selection, balanced trees, divide-and-conquer, pipelining, tree contraction, Euler tour; Parallel graph algorithms: Connected components, coloring, MST, shortest paths; Asynchronous models, NC-reductions, P-completeness.

title: CSL515 Randomized Algorithms (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL515 - Randomized Algorithms (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 6, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Introduction and basic tools: random sequences, pseudorandom generation, statistical tests (Chi-square); Game theoretic techniques: Yao principle; Moments and deviations: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities, Chernoff bounds, Martingales; Tail bounds applications; Randomized graph algorithms: Min-cut, random walks, Markov chains; Probabilistic method and derandomization.

title: CSL612 Introduction to Computational Complexity (Part 1)
text: Course: CSL612 - Introduction to Computational Complexity (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 7, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Computational models, Turing Machines, Decidability, Reducibility; Time and Space Complexity, Time and Space Hierarchy Theorems; Non-deterministic computation, P vs NP, NP-completeness; Diagonalization limits; Oracle Turing Machines and the Relativization barrier; Space complexity classes (L, NL, PSPACE); Boolean circuits and Circuit Complexity.

title: CSL612 Introduction to Computational Complexity (Part 2)
text: Course: CSL612 - Introduction to Computational Complexity (Computer Science and Engineering). Semester 7, 3.0 Credits. Topics: Randomized complexity classes (RP, BPP, ZPP).

title: Rule: RULE_GRAD_CREDITS_TOTAL
text: Academic Policy [GRADUATION]: A student must accumulate a minimum of 144 academic credits plus 12 non-graded core units for the award of the BTech degree in Computer Science and Engineering. (Threshold: 144.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_GRAD_NON_GRADED_UNITS
text: Academic Policy [GRADUATION]: A student must earn 12 units of non-graded core (NC) courses through prescribed formal and informal co-curricular activities (including NCN100 Wellbeing and NSS/NSO). (Threshold: 12.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_INSTITUTE_CORE_CREDITS
text: Academic Policy [CURRICULUM_DISTRIBUTION]: Students in BTech CSE must complete a minimum of 40.5 credits of Institute Core (IC) courses. (Threshold: 40.5, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_PROGRAM_CORE_CREDITS
text: Academic Policy [CURRICULUM_DISTRIBUTION]: Students in BTech CSE must complete a minimum of 52 credits of Program Core (PC) courses. (Threshold: 52.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_PROGRAM_ELECTIVE_CREDITS
text: Academic Policy [CURRICULUM_DISTRIBUTION]: Students in BTech CSE must complete a minimum of 22.5 credits of Program Elective (PE) courses. (Threshold: 22.5, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_OPEN_ELECTIVE_CREDITS
text: Academic Policy [CURRICULUM_DISTRIBUTION]: Students in BTech CSE must complete a minimum of 15 credits of Open Elective (OE) courses. (Threshold: 15.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_LIBERAL_ARTS_CREDITS
text: Academic Policy [CURRICULUM_DISTRIBUTION]: Students in BTech CSE must complete a minimum of 10 credits of Liberal Arts (LA) courses. (Threshold: 10.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_MAX_SEMESTER_CREDIT_LOAD
text: Academic Policy [CREDIT_LIMIT]: The standard maximum semester credit registration is bounded by the curriculum template load, typically not exceeding 22.0 credits per regular semester. (Threshold: 22.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_MIN_SEMESTER_CREDIT_LOAD
text: Academic Policy [CREDIT_LIMIT]: A student must register for a minimum course load of 12.0 credits in any regular semester to maintain full-time undergraduate standing. (Threshold: 12.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)

title: Rule: RULE_PREREQUISITE_PASS_GRADE
text: Academic Policy [PREREQUISITES]: Each course may specify prerequisite courses. A student who has obtained an F, FS, I, or X grade in a prerequisite course is not eligible to register for the course. (Threshold: 4.0, Applies to: all courses)

title: Rule: RULE_COURSE_OVERLAP_LIMIT
text: Academic Policy [REGISTRATION]: If a course has more than 25% overlapping content with another course already credited by the student, the student is not eligible to register for that course. (Threshold: 25.0, Applies to: all courses)

title: Rule: RULE_NPTEL_MAX_CREDIT_LIMIT
text: Academic Policy [ONLINE_CREDITS]: BTech students can take V-type courses (lectures by external experts or approved NPTEL courses, 1-2 credits each, running >= 1 month) up to a maximum of 6 credits during the entire program. (Threshold: 6.0, Applies to: BTech)

title: Rule: RULE_CREDIT_VALIDITY_LIFETIME
text: Academic Policy [CREDIT_VALIDITY]: The credits earned for any course are valid for up to 7 years only and shall not be counted towards degree requirements if acquired earlier than 7 years. (Threshold: 7.0, Applies to: all courses)

title: Rule: RULE_MIN_FIRST_CLASS_CGPA
text: Academic Policy [GRADUATION]: For employment or external certification requirements, an IIT Bhilai graduate having 6.0 CGPA and above is certified as First Class. (Threshold: 6.0, Applies to: BTech CSE)
